findings.body: `latestMeta` is taken from only the first restored worker, but the retirement patch is then applied to every `expectedWorkers` entry. With mixed legacy metadata, a pending first worker causes an already-`applied` sibling to be rewritten as `blocked` with `patch_flow_retired`, violating preservation of historical status. If the already-applied worker is first, the guard is skipped and the function can proceed to start a verifier while another worker remains pending. Decide from all worker statuses and patch only pending legacy entries.
findings.title: [P1] Inspect all legacy worker statuses before blocking

overall_explanation: The patch removes the retired proposal-only worker path and deferred candidate application, and the catalog/UI retirement projection is aligned. The completion guard is order-dependent for restored metadata with mixed worker statuses, so it can corrupt already-applied records or start verification while a sibling remains pending; this violates the retirement and historical-effect preservation contract.
